mainTopic: How תפילין are built: the compartments, the parchments, switching head and arm תפילין, and the order of the פרשיות
overview: This amud is all about how תפילין are built. First, רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא give two sources for why the head-תפילין have four compartments. Next, a ברייתא teaches from 'זכרון' (one memorial) that the four פרשיות go on four parchments inside compartments made from one hide, and it discusses spacing, separating threads and visible grooves. A second ברייתא says the arm-תפילין are written on one parchment. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about whether four separate parchments must be attached, and רבא concludes that רבי יהודה changed his mind. The גמרא then asks how head-תפילין may be turned into arm-תפילין, since we do not lower קדושה. It answers that this is allowed only with new תפילין, or with a condition made from the start. Finally, a ברייתא sets the order of the four פרשיות, אביי settles a contradiction about right and left, and רב rules that switching the order makes the תפילין פסול. אביי's limit on that ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Four mentions of טוטפות teach four compartments
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל counts the spellings of טוטפות in three פסוקים: two are singular and one is plural. That adds up to four, so the head-תפילין need four compartments.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'לטטפת,' 'לטטפת,' 'לטוטפות.' That makes four. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives רבי ישמעאל's source for why the head-תפילין have four compartments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word appears three times in the תורה. Two times it is spelled without a ו, so it reads as singular and counts as one each. The third time it is spelled with a ו, so it reads as plural and counts as two. One plus one plus two equals four compartments.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For totefet', spelled short, without a ו, so it reads as singular
'For totafot', spelled full, with a ו, so it reads as plural
The head-תפילין, which have four separate compartments

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count the word three times just because it appears in three פסוקים. The plural spelling counts as two, so the total is four.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'For totefet,' 'for totefet,' 'for totafot' —
phrases.notes: שמות 13:16, דברים 6:8, דברים 11:18. The first two are written without a ו, so they read as singular; the last one has a ו, so it reads as plural.

phrases.english: here there are four,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The head-תפילין have four compartments, learned from four counted mentions of טוטפות.

steps.title: The word טוטפות itself means four
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the counting is not needed. The word טוטפות is made of two foreign words that each mean 'two', so together it means four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: This is not needed. 'טט' in the language of כתפי means two, and 'פת' in the language of אפריקי means two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different source for the same rule of four compartments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל agree that there are four compartments. They only disagree about the source. For רבי עקיבא, the word טוטפות is a combination of 'טט' (two) and 'פת' (two), which makes four.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. He means the proof from counting is unnecessary.
A word meaning 'two' in the language of Katfi
A word meaning 'two' in the language of Afriki
Katfi, a foreign place or language
Afriki, a foreign place or language

steps.whyThisMatters: Both תנאים reach the same practical rule of four compartments. Only the source is in dispute.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: It is not needed;
'tat' in Katfi means two,
'pat' in Afriki means two.
phrases.notes: Put טט and פת together and you get טוטפות, which means two plus two, or four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four compartments are learned from the meaning of the word טוטפות itself.

steps.title: One memorial, not several
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא considers making four completely separate units. It rejects this using the פסוק 'ולזכרון', which teaches that the תפילין must be one memorial.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One might think he should write them on four hides and place them in four compartments made of four hides. The פסוק says, 'and for a memorial between your eyes.' I told you one memorial, not two or three memorials.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests a possible idea (four totally separate pieces) and then knocks it down with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זכרון is singular, so the head-תפילין must form one unit. This means the outer compartments cannot be four separate leather boxes. Exactly how to make it work is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought. This introduces an idea that will be rejected.
A memorial. The singular form shows the תפילין are one unit.
Hides, meaning pieces of parchment or leather

phrases.english: The Sages taught: One might think he should write them
on four hides,
and place them in four compartments made of four hides?
The verse teaches: 'And for a memorial between your eyes,'
one memorial I told you,
and not two or three memorials.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל יִכְתְּבֵם עַל אַרְבָּעָה עוֹרוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The head-תפילין must be one unit, not several separate memorials.

steps.title: Four parchments inside one leather housing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the practical method: write on four separate parchments, but make the four compartments from one piece of leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? He writes them on four hides and places them in four compartments made of one hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how to apply the 'one memorial' rule and gives the correct way to make the תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ideas are kept. There are four separate compartments, and there is also one unit. Each פרשה gets its own parchment, while the outer box is formed from a single hide.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? This introduces how the rule works in practice.
One hide, the single piece of leather the compartments are made from

steps.whatToRemember: The standard method: four parchments, four compartments, all from one leather housing.

phrases.english: How so?
He writes them on four hides
and places them in four compartments made of one hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the 'one memorial' principle into a practical method
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Write the פרשיות on four separate parchments and place them in four compartments formed from one hide.

steps.title: All four פרשיות on one parchment: a dispute about spacing
steps.stepSummary: If all four פרשיות were written on one parchment and placed in four compartments, the person has fulfilled the מצוה. רבי requires a space between the פרשיות; חכמים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he wrote them on one hide and placed them in four compartments, he has fulfilled his obligation. There must be a space between them; these are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: It is not necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא discusses a case where the regular method was not followed, rules that it still works, and records a מחלוקת about one detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing on one parchment is not the right way to start, but afterward it is valid (יצא). רבי says the פרשיות must have a gap between them so the parchment can be split into the four compartments. חכמים say no such gap is required.

keyTerms.meaning: He has fulfilled his obligation, even though this was not the right way to start

phrases.english: And if he wrote them on one hide,
and placed them in four compartments — he has fulfilled his obligation,
and there must be a space between them,
these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: It is not necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Handles the case where the method from step 4 was not followed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One parchment in four compartments is valid afterward; רבי requires a space between the פרשיות and חכמים do not.

steps.title: Both agree: a separating thread and visible grooves
steps.stepSummary: רבי and חכמים agree that a thread or band goes between each compartment, and that if the grooves between compartments cannot be seen, the תפילין are invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that one places a thread or a band between each and every one. And if their grooves are not noticeable, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by stating what both sides agree on, and adds a rule that makes the תפילין invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though they argue about a space on the parchment, both sides require a physical divider between the compartments. On the outside, the separation lines must be visible. Without them, the four compartments do not look like four, and the תפילין are פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree. This shows what both sides accept.
A band, thicker than a thread
Their grooves, the lines between the compartments

steps.whatToRemember: The four compartments must be separated inside by a thread or band, and the grooves must be visible from outside, or else the תפילין are פסול.

phrases.english: And they agree
that one places a thread or a band
between each and every one.
And if their grooves are not noticeable — they are invalid.
phrases.notes: The grooves are the lines on the outside of the box that show where one compartment ends and the next begins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States what both sides of the step 5 dispute agree on
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A thread or band must separate the compartments, and the grooves must be visible from outside, or the תפילין are invalid.

steps.title: The arm-תפילין go on one parchment, but four parchments still work
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the arm-תפילין are written on one hide. If they were written on four hides and put in one compartment, the person is יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: How does one write them? The arm-תפילין are written on one hide. If he wrote it on four hides and put it in one compartment, he has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a new ברייתא about the arm-תפילין, which are different from the head-תפילין we discussed before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head-תפילין have four compartments and four parchments, but the arm-תפילין have just one compartment. So the right way is to write all four פרשיות on one parchment. After the fact, four separate parchments in that one compartment are still valid.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: How does one write them?

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל יָד כּוֹתְבָהּ עַל עוֹר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: The arm-tefillin: he writes it on one hide,
and if he wrote it on four hides
and placed it in one compartment, he has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: "After the fact" is the point here: four parchments are not the ideal way, but they still work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the head-תפילין (four parchments, four compartments) to the arm-תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally the arm-תפילין are written on one parchment, but four parchments in one compartment are valid after the fact.

steps.title: Must the four parchments be attached?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if four parchments were used, they must be attached together, because the arm-תפילין must be one sign inside as well as outside. רבי יוסי says attaching is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He must attach them, as it says: 'And it shall be for a sign for you upon your arm.' Just as it is one sign on the outside, so too it must be one sign on the inside. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: it is not necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with an argument about the case of four parchments: do they need to be joined together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learns from the פסוק that the arm-תפילין are 'a sign', in the singular. The box outside is one piece, so the writing inside must also be one unit, which means gluing the four parchments together. רבי יוסי does not require this.

phrases.english: And he must attach them,
as it says: "And it shall be for a sign for you upon your arm,"
just as it is one sign on the outside,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אוֹת אַחַת מִבִּפְנִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: so too it must be one sign on the inside; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: It is not necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a מחלוקת about the four-parchment case from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: four parchments must be attached, based on 'לאות'. רבי יוסי: no attaching is needed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי says רבי יהודה agrees head-תפילין can serve as arm-תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי claims that רבי יהודה agrees with him in one case: someone who has two head-תפילין and no arm-תפילין may cover one of them with leather and wear it on his arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: רבי יהודה the distinguished agrees with me that if someone has no arm-תפילין but has two head-תפילין, he covers one of them with leather and puts it on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a case where, he says, רבי יהודה agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Head-תפילין have four separate parchments in four compartments. Wrapping the box in leather makes it look like one compartment from the outside, but the four parchments inside stay separate and are not attached. That is exactly the kind of case they argued about.

keyTerms.meaning: A title of honor: 'the distinguished one'
Covers or patches it with a piece of leather

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וּמוֹדֶה לִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרִיבִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: And Rabbi Yehuda the distinguished agrees with me

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אֵין לוֹ תְּפִילִּין שֶׁל יָד
phrases.english: that if he has no arm-tefillin

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי תְּפִילִּין שֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: but he has two head-tefillin,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁטּוֹלֶה עוֹר עַל אַחַת מֵהֶן וּמַנִּיחָהּ.
phrases.english: he covers one of them with leather and puts it on.
phrases.notes: The leather wrapping makes the four boxes look like a single compartment, and he wears it on his arm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וּמוֹדֶה לִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרִיבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי adds a case where he says his opponent agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Head-תפילין covered with leather may be worn as arm-תפילין, and רבי יוסי says רבי יהודה agrees.

steps.title: How can רבי יהודה agree to this? It is their very argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's claim. The head-תפילין case has four unattached parchments, which is exactly what רבי יהודה rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: He agrees? That is exactly what they argue about!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that רבי יוסי says רבי יהודה agrees here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said four parchments for the arm must be attached. Covered head-תפילין still hold four separate parchments. So רבי יהודה should not allow this case.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the very point they disagree about

phrases.english: He agrees? That is exactly their dispute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 9 using the argument in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that רבי יהודה agrees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case has four unattached parchments, which רבי יהודה requires to be attached. So he cannot agree.

steps.title: רבא: רבי יהודה changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יוסי's statement shows רבי יהודה took back his opinion and accepted רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From רבי יוסי's words we learn that רבי יהודה retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by saying רבי יהודה later accepted רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no hidden difference between the two cases. 'Agrees with me' means רבי יהודה came around to רבי יוסי's position that attaching is not required.
steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי יהודה accepted רבי יוסי's view: four unattached parchments in the arm-תפילין are acceptable.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מִדְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rava said: From the words of Rabbi Yosei
we learn that Rabbi Yehuda retracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִדְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי חָזַר בּוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה still holds the parchments must be attached, so 'agrees' makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה retracted and now agrees with רבי יוסי.

steps.title: But head-תפילין may not be lowered into arm-תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that head-תפילין can become arm-תפילין. רבי יוחנן ruled that arm-תפילין can become head-תפילין, but not the other way, because we do not lower something from higher קדושה to lower קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב חנניה sent in the name of רבי יוחנן: arm-תפילין may be made into head-תפילין, but head-תפילין may not be made into arm-תפילין, because we do not lower something from greater holiness to lesser holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks a different part of רבי יוסי's case: the very idea of turning head-תפילין into arm-תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Head-תפילין have more קדושה than arm-תפילין. רבי יוחנן says you may move up in holiness but not down. רבי יוסי's case moves down, so it seems forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: This question is not about the parchments being attached. It is a new problem about lowering the holiness of the head-תפילין.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rav Ḥananya sent
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל יָד עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָהּ שֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: Arm-tefillin may be made into head-tefillin,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל רֹאשׁ אֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָהּ שֶׁל יָד,
phrases.english: but head-tefillin may not be made into arm-tefillin,
because we do not lower
from greater holiness to lesser holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא שְׁלַח רַב חֲנַנְיָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to step 9's case and challenges it from a different angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission in step 9 to use head-תפילין as arm-תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן forbids lowering from greater to lesser קדושה, and head to arm is a lowering.

steps.title: Old תפילין versus new תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's rule is about old תפילין that were already worn on the head. רבי יוסי's case is about new ones that were never used.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is about old תפילין, and that one is about new תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ruling is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once head-תפילין have been worn, they have the higher קדושה of the head, and they cannot be lowered. New head-תפילין that were never worn have not yet received that status, so they may be used on the arm.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about old tefillin,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's rule: they were already worn on the head.

phrases.english: that one is about new tefillin.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי's case: they were never worn yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּעַתִּיקָתָא, הָא בְּחַדְתָּתָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): old versus new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any head-תפילין carry head-level קדושה and cannot be lowered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only head-תפילין that were already worn are locked into the higher קדושה. New ones may be used on the arm.

steps.title: If designation counts, he made a condition from the start
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that designating an object already gives it קדושה, even new head-תפילין would be holy. So רבי יוסי's case must be one where the person made a condition from the start that he could switch them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says designation counts: it is a case where he made a condition about them from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adjusts its answer so that it also works for the view that הזמנה, setting something aside for a מצוה, already creates holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הזמנה counts, new head-תפילין are already holy just from being made for the head, so the old/new answer is not enough. The case must be one where he stated from the beginning that he might use them for the arm. That condition stops them from being locked into head-level קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: Designating an item for a מצוה is significant and gives it status

steps.whatToRemember: Head-תפילין may be used as arm-תפילין only if they were never worn. According to the view that הזמנה counts, they must also have been made with a condition from the start.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how הזמנה and a תנאי decide when an object for a מצוה takes on its קדושה.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says designation is significant,
it is where he made a condition about them from the start.
phrases.notes: He said at the outset that these head-תפילין might be used for the arm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the answer of step 13 for the view that הזמנה creates holiness.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case further: a condition made at the start
steps.terutzHavaAmina: New תפילין are always free to be switched.
steps.terutzMaskana: If הזמנה counts, switching is allowed only when he made a condition from the beginning.

steps.title: The order of the four passages in the תפילין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that קדש לי and והיה כי יביאך go on the right, and שמע and והיה אם שמוע go on the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: How are the passages arranged? 'קדש לי' and 'והיה כי יביאך' go on the right. 'שמע' and 'והיה אם שמוע' go on the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that tells us where each of the four פרשיות sits inside the תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four פרשיות in תפילין. The two from ספר שמות (קדש לי and והיה כי יביאך) go on one side, the right. The two from ספר דברים (שמע and והיה אם שמוע) go on the other side, the left.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How is their order?
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the four פרשיות that go inside the תפילין.

phrases.english: "Sanctify unto Me" and "And it shall be when He brings you" are on the right,
"Listen" and "And it shall come to pass if you shall hearken" are on the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The previous discussion was about switching head-תפילין and arm-תפילין, and this step moves on to the order of the פרשיות inside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שמות passages go on the right and the דברים passages go on the left.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a ברייתא that reverses the order, putting the שמות passages on the left and the דברים passages on the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא by bringing a second ברייתא that swaps right and left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות seem to argue about which side each pair of פרשיות goes on. The גמרא needs to explain how both can be right.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught the opposite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 15 with a ברייתא that seems to contradict it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The right/left arrangement in the ברייתא of step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא gives the reverse arrangement, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי: the reader's right compared with the wearer's right
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that one ברייתא means the right side of a person facing the wearer, and the other means the wearer's own right side. Either way, the facing reader reads the פרשיות in the order they appear in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no difficulty. Here it means the reader's right. There it means the right of the one wearing them. And the reader reads them in their order.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by showing that the two ברייתות describe the same arrangement from two different points of view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone standing face to face with the wearer has his right side where the wearer's left side is. So 'right' in one ברייתא and 'left' in the other point to the same spot. Seen this way, a person facing the wearer reads the passages in the same order they appear in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really conflict
The reader, the person standing opposite the wearer
The one putting on the תפילין
In their order, the order they appear in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות do not argue. They describe one arrangement, but they count 'right' from two different people who face each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: The words 'the reader reads them in their order' became the basis for a famous disagreement between רש"י and רבנו תם about the exact arrangement of the פרשיות in תפילין.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult,
here it means to the right of the reader,
phrases.notes: The 'reader' is someone facing the wearer and looking at his תפילין.

phrases.english: there it means to the right of the one wearing them,
and the reader reads them in their order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different points of view: the two sources count 'right' from different people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות argue about which side the passages go on.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree. One counts from the reader's right and the other from the wearer's right, and the facing reader sees the passages in Torah order.

steps.title: Switching the order of the passages makes the תפילין פסול
steps.stepSummary: רב חננאל in the name of רב rules that if the פרשיות were put in the wrong order, the תפילין are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חננאל said in the name of רב: If he switched its passages, they are פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the correct order, רב teaches that this order is required: putting the פרשיות in a different order makes the תפילין פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order from the ברייתא is not just the preferred way. It is a requirement, so getting it wrong invalidates the תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: The written passages inside the תפילין

phrases.english: Rav Ḥananel says that Rav says:
If one exchanged its passages, they are unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the arrangement just set out and rules that departing from it makes the תפילין פסול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין whose פרשיות are in the wrong order are פסול.

steps.title: אביי begins to limit רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens with 'we did not say this,' which signals that he is about to narrow when רב's ruling applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We did not say this...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. אביי is getting ready to limit רב's rule, and the details of his limitation come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'We did not say' tells us that רב's ruling does not cover every kind of switch. Only some cases will be פסול, and אביי is about to explain which ones.

keyTerms.meaning: We did not say this; it introduces a limit on an earlier ruling

phrases.english: Abaye said: We did not say this

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to narrow the ruling of רב in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling has a limit; the details continue on the next amud.
